official.deadline_central_display: Set by each Japanese diplomatic mission; call opens around mid-April 2026
official.deadline_note: MEXT does not publish a single closing date. The application guidelines state that the call for applications opens at each Japanese diplomatic mission around mid-April 2026 and that the deadline for submission of application documents varies according to each Japanese diplomatic mission, so you must confirm it on the mission's own website. The placement preference application form is due around mid-September to early October 2026.
official.application_cycle: 2027 intake - first screening May to late July 2026, results January to March 2027, arrival in April or October 2027
official.status_note: The application guidelines page on mext.go.jp is published as the CURRENT version of the 2027 (Research Students) guidelines, and the flow shows the call opening at each Japanese diplomatic mission around mid-April 2026.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Fees for the entrance examination, matriculation, and tuition at universities are waived; the entrance examination fee is borne by the grantee if they cannot proceed to the master's or doctoral course or cannot be admitted to the university.
benefits: Monthly allowance of 143,000 yen for students receiving preparatory education and non-regular students.
Monthly allowance of 144,000 yen for regular students enrolled in master's or professional degree courses.
Monthly allowance of 145,000 yen for regular students enrolled in doctoral courses.
A supplemental regional allowance of 2,000 yen or 3,000 yen per month for grantees studying or conducting research in specially designated regions.
Education fees: fees for the entrance examination, matriculation, and tuition at universities are waived.
Traveling expenses: an economy-class airline ticket provided for transportation to Japan and back.
eligibility: Nationality: applicants must have the nationality of a country that has diplomatic relations with Japan; applicants holding Japanese nationality at the time of application are not eligible.
Age: applicants, in principle, must have been born on or after April 2, 1992.

Japanese language: applicants must be willing to learn Japanese, must be interested in Japan and be willing to deepen their understanding of Japan after arriving, and must have the ability to conduct research and adapt to living in Japan.
Health: applicants must submit a health certificate in the prescribed format signed by a physician attesting that the applicant has no physical or mental conditions hindering study in Japan.

Arrival in Japan: applicants must choose either the April term (arriving between April 1 and April 7, 2027) or the October term (arriving within the period specified by the accepting university within two weeks before or after the start of its academic term).

Non-eligibility: military personnel or civilian employees at arrival or during payment, those who cannot arrive in the specified period, previous grantees of MEXT scholarship programs (subject to exceptions), those applying to another MEXT program, those already enrolled or planning to enrol as privately-financed international students, those planning to receive other Japanese-government scholarships, and those found to have cheated in the first screening are ineligible.
requirements: Academic background: applicants must satisfy one of the conditions for admission to either a master's or doctoral course at the Japanese graduate school they wish to first enrol in, including completion of 16 years of school education or a three-year university programme with a degree equivalent to a bachelor's.
Medical certificate in the prescribed 2027 form.
Field of Study and Research Plan on the 2027 form.
Academic transcript for all academic years of university attended, issued by the university or the applicant's national government.
Certification of graduation or prospective graduation from the university attended.
Abstracts of theses, if the applicant has written theses; certificate of language proficiency only if issued no earlier than two years before application.
documents: Application Form, 2027 form, one original and two copies.
Placement Preference Application Form, 2027 form, one original and two copies.
Field of Study and Research Plan, 2027 form, one original and two copies.
Academic transcript for all academic years of university attended.
Certification of graduation or degree certificate of the university attended, or a certificate of prospective graduation.
Recommendation letter from the president/dean or the academic advisor at the current or last university attended, free format.
Medical certificate on the 2027 certificate form.
Abstracts of theses, three copies, if the applicant has written theses.
Certificate of language proficiency, three copies, only if held and issued no earlier than two years before application.
selection_criteria: First screening conducted by the Japanese diplomatic mission, generally a written examination, interview and academic records.
Second screening and university placement conducted by MEXT, based on first screening results and the Placement Preference Application Form.
Applicants must pass the first screening and then directly contact the Japanese universities they wish to enrol in to request provisional acceptance.
coverage: Monthly allowance of 143,000 yen for students receiving preparatory education and non-regular students, 144,000 yen for regular students in master's or professional degree courses, and 145,000 yen for regular students in doctoral courses.
Additional regional allowance of 2,000 or 3,000 yen per month in specially designated regions.
Education fees: fees for the entrance examination, matriculation, and tuition at universities are waived.
Traveling expenses: an economy-class airline ticket for transportation to Japan, provided to grantees who arrive during the specified period.
Granted a scholarship period lasting from the arrival month until the standard period of study, extendable for advanced study upon successful examination by MEXT.
application_method: Confirm the application deadline and required documents at the Japanese diplomatic mission in your country of nationality.
Submit the application documents to the Japanese diplomatic mission by the designated deadline.
Pass the first screening, then directly contact Japanese universities to request provisional acceptance.
Submit a completed Placement Preference Application Form to the Japanese diplomatic mission, around mid-September to early October 2026.
MEXT conducts second screening and university placement from November 2026, with results notified January to March 2027.
official.application_route: Apply through the Japanese diplomatic mission in your country of nationality by its own published deadline; the scholarship is awarded by MEXT after first screening, provisional university acceptance, placement preference and second screening.
official.study_mode: Full-time enrolment in a master's, doctoral or professional graduate course at a Japanese graduate school, or research at an undergraduate department, graduate school or institute attached to a university.
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants must hold the nationality of a country that has diplomatic relations with Japan. Applicants holding Japanese nationality at the time of application are not eligible; dual nationals who hold Japanese nationality and reside outside Japan at application may apply if they choose the nationality of the other country and relinquish Japanese nationality by arrival.
official.international_eligibility: This scheme is exclusively for international students who are nationals of countries having diplomatic relations with Japan and who apply through the Japanese diplomatic mission in the country of their nationality.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Applicants should apply for the field of study they majored in at university or its related fields. Traditional entertainment arts such as Kabuki and classical Japanese dances, and subjects requiring practical training at factories or companies, are not included. Fields of study may be restricted by each Japanese diplomatic mission.
official.research_requirement: Applicants must be enrolled in a master's, doctoral or professional graduate course at a graduate school, or be conducting research in a specialised field with the aim of completing the course.
official.duration: Non-regular students: April 2027 (or September/October 2027) until the end of March 2029, with the first 6-month period devoted to preparatory education where required. Regular students: the necessary period for completion of the respective regular course, with a 6-month preparatory education period where the accepting university deems it necessary.
official.description: The Japanese Government (Monbukagakusho) Scholarship Program, administered by the Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT) of Japan, offers scholarships to international students who wish to study in graduate courses at Japanese universities as Research Students, with the stated aim of fostering human resources who will become bridges of friendship between the grantee's country and Japan and contribute to the development of both countries and the wider world.
official.english_requirement: No English requirement is published; applicants must be willing to learn Japanese, and Japanese language proficiency certificates only qualify as optional supporting documents.

not_confirmed: deadline_central - MEXT publishes no single deadline; the application guidelines state the deadline varies according to each Japanese diplomatic mission
funding_amount as a single value - MEXT publishes three course-dependent monthly allowances of 143,000, 144,000 and 145,000 yen, so the recorded figure is the lowest of the three
medical examination, return-home obligations, re-eligibility and interview details - these are set mission by mission and are not published in the guidelines
verification.notes: The official 2027 (Research Students) application guidelines PDF on mext.go.jp was read in full. The three monthly allowance figures, the 2,000 and 3,000 yen regional supplement, the waiver of entrance examination, matriculation and tuition fees, the economy-class ticket, the April and October arrival windows, the standard period of study and the mission-set deadline were all confirmed on the awarding body's own domain. The identical figures appear on the Study in Japan official site.

applicant_utility.summary: This is genuinely full funding: entrance examination, matriculation and tuition fees are waived, you get an economy-class air ticket and a monthly allowance of 143,000 yen rising to 144,000 or 145,000 yen once you are a regular master's or doctoral student, with 2,000 or 3,000 yen extra if you are placed in one of the specially designated regions. The single most important practical point is that there is no central deadline - each Japanese embassy or consulate sets its own, so your embassy's website is your only reliable source for the closing date and document list. Start by securing provisional acceptance from a Japanese university once you pass the first screening, because MEXT does the placement itself from November.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Graduates under 35 who want a funded master's or doctoral research degree at a Japanese university and are prepared to learn Japanese and adapt to living in Japan.
application_readiness_checklist: Check the age rule: in principle you must have been born on or after April 2, 1992.
Go to the Japanese diplomatic mission in your country of nationality and note its own deadline, since MEXT sets none centrally.
Confirm your chosen field of study is not traditional entertainment arts such as Kabuki or classical Japanese dance, and is not restricted by your mission.
Decide between the April term and the October term before you submit, because in principle the choice cannot be changed afterwards.

Assemble the required documents on the 2027 forms: physician-signed health certificate, transcripts for every university year, graduation certificate, and a free-format recommendation letter from your dean or advisor.
After passing first screening, contact Japanese universities directly to request provisional acceptance, then submit the Placement Preference Application Form to your mission.
common_rejection_risks: Being already enrolled, or planning to enrol, in a Japanese university as a privately-financed international student from the time of application until the scholarship payment period starts.
Being a previous grantee of any MEXT scholarship program, which is an automatic bar unless the three-year exception applies.
Planning to receive another scholarship from the Japanese government or a government-related organisation, or simultaneously applying under another MEXT program.
Failing to arrive in Japan within the specified April or October window, in which case travel expenses are not paid and the scholarship is withdrawn.
Changing residence status away from Student after arrival, which suspends payment.
Cheating during the first screening written examination, or having no intention of obtaining a degree in Japan, both disqualify you outright.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Domestic travel within Japan, airport taxes, special taxes, travel insurance, carry-on luggage or unaccompanied baggage expenses, and travel costs beyond the economy-class ticket MEXT provides. You also bear the entrance examination fee if you cannot proceed to the master's or doctoral course or cannot be admitted to the university.
document_audit: The Application Form, Placement Preference Application Form, Field of Study and Research Plan and Medical certificate must all be the 2027 forms - last year's version is a common mistake.
The transcript must cover all academic years of university attended and be issued by the university attended or your national government.
The language proficiency certificate only counts if issued no earlier than two years before application, and is optional.
Abstracts of theses are submitted in three copies and only if you have written theses; the medical certificate requires a physician's signature.
The recommendation letter is free format, so do not wait for a prescribed template.
alerts: There is no central deadline: the guidelines state the deadline for submission of application documents varies according to each Japanese diplomatic mission.
Military personnel and military civilian employees are ineligible both at arrival and throughout the payment period.
Applications cannot be made simultaneously with another program under the Japanese Government Scholarship system, including programs whose payments begin in FY2026.
The scholarship is suspended if a grantee is absent from the university for an extended period, and may be reduced or repaid after false statements or other violations.
Arrival choice between the April and October terms is fixed at application in principle; changing it is not permitted.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: You apply with all documents to the Japanese diplomatic mission in your country of nationality by its own deadline, pass the first screening there, request provisional acceptance directly from Japanese universities, submit the Placement Preference Application Form to your mission by around mid-September to early October, and MEXT then conducts second screening and university placement from November with results notified January to March 2027.
